claims.statement: The YAML files under resources/settings are the canonical setting metadata; the generated master.conf and setting_inputs.conf are derived artifacts embedded as Qt resources and loaded by SettingsManager.
The settings generator validates required fields, types, dependencies, enum defaults, duplicate names, and composite-input component consistency before emitting deterministic JSON.
CMake watches the settings YAML and generator, regenerates both configuration outputs, and makes the main object target depend on the generation target when automatic generation is enabled.
SettingsManager initializes the active global base from master defaults and overlays selected sparse .s2c templates, with LFAM_03in as the missing-template fallback.
Planar slicing composes effective settings in global, part, matching layer-range, and local-adjustment order before cross-sectioning.
Settings meshes are cross-sectioned into SettingsPolygon objects, and region generation can split paths at polygon boundaries and overlay polygon-local values into segment settings.
The settings UI chooses row widgets from generated type metadata, supports composite vector rows, and hides non-local rows while a local settings base is being edited.

Older setting files can be rolled forward automatically or after a GUI or console prompt; accepting a file-based template migration rewrites the document, while declining currently does not stop the loader from inspecting its settings.

Focused migration tests cover historical helical angle-to-arc-length conversion, variable-Z enum conversion, connected-contour key renames, preservation of current keys on collisions, idempotence, and advancement to master version 15.
Preference import blocks intermediate signals while applying the complete file, then emits one aggregate unit-change notification whose observers see the final imported state.
Preferences are application-local state with compiled fallbacks; missing fields keep their current values, a missing preferences file marks defaults dirty, and export clears the dirty flag.

SettingsManager rejects unreadable JSON and documents that do not have the settings-template shape before version migration or template population, preventing project sidecars from being loaded as global templates.

The settings-file comparator validates both settings documents, compares corresponding settings-array entries by index, reports changed and one-sided keys, performs recursive object comparison independent of object key order, and applies a floating-point tolerance while retaining exact non-float comparison.
The settings comparison dialog requires two selected files, then presents changed values and one-sided values in separate sortable tables with settings-set indexes and master-catalog display names.
SettingsBase normalizes connected-contour legacy keys for unversioned JSON imports and overlays; connected enable flags allow local scope but chain control options are global-only.
SettingsManager restores the original document after migration exceptions and returns -1; preference color migration maps SpiralConnection to Connection while retaining an existing Connection value.
Template reload replaces cached keys/categories, while separately tracked applied keys allow switching away to reset keys removed since application.
Template activation optionally prompts to apply every available category, while reselecting the current single-category template preserves manual edits.
Grouped settings forms use region/section metadata, hide empty groups, and force matching regions open during search; ARC Gas Timing uses one field per row.
Override indicators collect differing part and layer-range values across the session, and scans can be suspended during project loading.
ARC wire-feed speed widgets are exempt from machine XY motion-speed limits.
Application themes provide explicit Light/Dark palettes with a Light default and bundled Noto Sans fonts.
